response: {"text":"The research looked at how much of a trapped contaminant could later be taken out of a carbon‑based filter for testing. The main factor examined was how fast water moved through the filter, measured as a flow per unit area, and whether raising this speed would noticeably lower the filter’s ability to capture organic substances. Because the intended use involved detecting trace amounts of organic chemicals in field samples, the study also considered how the initial contaminant level affected results. Extremely low levels (around one part per billion or less) are hard to handle in a lab, so most experiments used concentrations thousands of times higher and then projected the filter’s behavior at the very low levels by extending the observed trends."}
